# Chapter Eighteen: Kinship of Blood

Brock's claws were inches from Victor's throat when the high leaded-glass windows of the conservatory shattered in an explosion of crystalline shards.

A colossal silhouette—larger and broader than Brock, covered in jet-black fur that seemed to swallow the ambient light—dropped from the ceiling like a falling meteor, slamming into Brock mid-leap with the force of an artillery shell.

The impact drove Brock twenty feet across the library, shattering a massive mahogany desk into matchwood. The rogue alpha screamed in fury as the two massive apex predators tumbled across the floor in a ferocious tangle of snapping jaws, slashing claws, and splintering floorboards.

Victor scrambled backward, his back against the stone hearth, *Lobera* raised and humming with blue luminescence.

Two more wolves leaped through the shattered conservatory windows. One was a lean, auburn-furred female whose movements were a masterclass in lethal agility; the other was a massive gray enforcer with scarred flanks. In an instant, Rebecca and Marcus crashed into Martin and the remaining two berserkers.

The great hall of Dundee manor erupted into primeval war.

Rebecca moved like quicksilver, feinting low beneath a berserker's sweeping swipe and driving her jaws directly into the creature's femoral artery with crushing force. Marcus tackled the second berserker, using his immense bulk to drive the rogue into the stone fireplace, breaking its neck with a single sickening twist.

In the center of the room, Brock rolled frantically, kicking out with his hind legs to dislodge the black wolf pinned atop him. He scrambled to his feet, bleeding from deep gouges across his shoulder, his chest heaving with rabid exhaustion. His yellow eyes widened in shock as he recognized the towering black beast standing between him and Victor.

"Sowain!" Brock hissed, backing toward the shattered front entrance. "You traitor! You crossed the ocean to protect a human hunter? To protect the blade that slaughtered our ancestors?"

The black wolf did not roar or snarl. With a low, resonant growl that vibrated through the floorboards, the massive beast began to shift. Bones cracked and repositioned; thick black fur receded into smooth, scarred bronze skin; the lupine muzzle reformed into the stern, weathered features of Alfonso.

Within seconds, Alfonso stood tall in human form, wearing his torn woolen overcoat, his amber eyes fixed on Brock with absolute, chilling authority.

"You broke the covenant, Brock," Alfonso said, his voice deep, calm, and terrifyingly cold. "You attacked a family. You slaughtered innocents. You brought the butchers of Rome down upon every pack in the hemisphere. You are no longer of my blood. You are a rabid dog, and tonight, your hunt ends."

Martin, seeing that his fighters were dead and that the Alpha of Alphas stood before them, grabbed Brock's arm. "Brock! The transport! We can't take them here—fall back to Glen Clova!"

Brock glared at Alfonso with murderous hatred, then spat a mouthful of black blood onto the marble floor. "This isn't over, Sowain! When Mercer's gas fills the glen, you will all choke on your own blood!"

With a final, desperate leap, Brock and Martin vaulted through the ruined front entrance, vanishing into the torrential rain and the black Highland night. Outside, the roar of a high-performance diesel engine tore through the storm as their van accelerated down the driveway.

Marcus moved toward the door to pursue, but Alfonso held up a commanding hand. "Let them go, Marcus. They are running straight into Mercer's perimeter. We have more urgent business here."

The great hall fell into an eerie, heavy silence, broken only by the crackle of the dying hearth and the steady drum of rain pouring through the shattered windows.

Alfonso slowly turned around.

Victor stood twenty feet away, his breathing ragged, his knuckles white around the hilt of *Lobera*. The sword's blade was still bathed in crackling silver light, illuminating the blood spattered across Victor's clothes. His left hand gripped the Jamestown dagger, pointed squarely at Alfonso's chest.

For a long, agonizing moment, the two men stared at each other.

Victor looked at Alfonso's face. It was the face from the mirror. The face from the Jamestown visions. The young man who had stood in the Virginia snow in 1612, terrified of his first solo hunt, listening to his uncle's stern commands. The jawline was the same; the fiery blue-and-amber eyes were identical; only the gray in his beard and the deep lines of three hundred years of sorrow distinguished the legend from the memory.

Alfonso's gaze dropped to the weapons in Victor's hands. When his eyes locked onto *Lobera*, a profound, bittersweet emotion softened his rugged features. Slowly, deliberately, Alfonso raised his empty hands and took a single step forward.

"Lower the steel, Victor," Alfonso said softly, his voice trembling with an emotion he had kept buried for centuries. "I am Alfonso of Castile. You carry my uncle's blade, and my blood runs in your veins. We did not cross the Atlantic to harm you. We came to save your life."

Victor stared at him, his chest heaving, his mind spinning as the reality of the visions crashed into the physical world. Slowly, Victor released his breath, lowering the point of *Lobera* toward the floor.

From behind the shattered bookcase, a weak, gravelly groan broke the silence.

"Bloody hell..." Father Edgar wheezed, struggling to push a broken oak shelf off his chest. "Someone tell me... that wasn't the Queen's guard... coming to inspect the carpet..."

Rebecca shifted back into her human form, immediately rushing across the room to kneel beside the wounded priest. "He's bleeding heavily from a skull fracture, Alpha. Two broken ribs and internal contusions."

"Get him onto the sofa," Alfonso commanded gently, stepping toward the hearth. "We have thirty minutes before Mercer realizes his bait didn't die. Rebecca, tend to his wounds. Victor... it is time you learned the truth about why your ancestors forged that sword."

---
